text:
$K_{a_{1}}$, $K_{a_{2}}$ and $K_{a_{3}}$ are the respective ionization constants for the following reactions (a), (b) and (c).

(a) $H_{2}C_{2}O_{4}⇌H^{+}+HC_{2}O_{4}^{-}$

(b) $HC_{2}O_{4}^{-}⇌H^{+}+C_{2}O_{4}^{2-}$

(c) $H_{2}C_{2}O4⇌2H^{+}+C_{2}O_{4}^{2-}$

The relationship between $K_{a_{1}}$, $K_{a_{2}}$ and $K_{a_{3}}$ is given as :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}⇌2\mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-}\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{3}}$

$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}⇌\mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{HC}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{-}\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{1}}$

$\mathrm{HC}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{-}⇌\mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-}\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{2}}$

$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{3}}=\frac{[\mathrm{H}^{+}]^{2}\left [\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-}\right ]}{[\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}]}$

$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{1}}=\frac{[\mathrm{H}^{+}]\left [\mathrm{HC}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{-}\right ]}{[\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}]},\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{2}}=\frac{[\mathrm{H}^{+}]\left [\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-}\right ]}{\left [\mathrm{HC}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{-}\right ]}$

$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{3}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{1}}\times \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}_{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: The molar conductivity of a conductivity cell filled with 10 moles of 20 mL NaCl solution is $\Lambda _{m1}$ and that of 20 moles another identical cell having 80 mL NaCl solution is $\Lambda _{m2}$. sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}_{1}}=\frac{\mathrm{k}_{1}\times 1000}{\mathrm{M}_{1}}=\frac{\mathrm{k}\times 1000}{\frac{10}{0.02}}$

$\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{k}_{2}\times 1000}{\frac{20}{0.08}}$

It is given that $\mathrm{k}_{1}=\mathrm{k}_{2}$

Applying the given condition on conductivity.

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}_{1}}}{2}=\dfrac{\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}_{2}}}{4} \\ \Lambda _{\mathrm{m}_{2}}=2\Lambda _{\mathrm{m}_{1}} \end{array}$

text:
Major product of the following reaction is


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The reactant is allyl acrylate, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{COO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$. With 2 HBr and no peroxide, each $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ adds one HBr by ionic (electrophilic) addition.

Allyl part: this $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ is isolated, so Markovnikov's rule applies. $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ adds to the terminal $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$, giving the more stable secondary carbocation on the middle carbon, which $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ traps: $-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$.

Acrylate part: this $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ is conjugated with $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$. A carbocation on the $α$-carbon (the Markovnikov route) would sit next to the electron-withdrawing carbonyl group and is strongly destabilised. Instead $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ adds to the carbonyl oxygen, giving a cation delocalised onto the $β$-carbon; $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ attacks the $β$-carbon and the enol formed tautomerises (overall 1,4-addition). Br ends up on the terminal carbon: $\mathrm{BrCH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{COO}{}^{-}$.


[IMG]

The major product is $\mathrm{BrCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COOCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CHBrCH}{}_{3}$. Option (B) wrongly applies Markovnikov's rule to the double bond conjugated with the carbonyl group as well.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text:
What is the major product of the following reaction?


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
2-Methylpropanal, $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CHCHO}$, has one $α$-hydrogen, so aqueous $\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$ brings about aldol addition.

$\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$ removes the $α$-hydrogen to form the enolate (carbanion at C-2), which adds to the carbonyl carbon of a second molecule; the alkoxide formed takes a proton from water:

$2~(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CHCHO}{}_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}}^{\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}}\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$

The product is 3-hydroxy-2,2,4-trimethylpentanal. Its C-2 carries two methyl groups and no hydrogen, so the base-promoted dehydration of the aldol, which needs an $α$-hydrogen, cannot give the alkene of option (A); option (C) would need an oxidising agent, and option (D) has only six carbon atoms.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: In base vs. acid titration, at the end point methyl orange is present as
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Methyl orange, ${}_{}^{}{}_{}^{-}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$, is yellow in neutral or basic solution, where it has the benzenoid (azo) structure with both rings aromatic.

In acidic solution it takes up $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ on the azo nitrogen; the $-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{N}=$ group and $=\mathrm{N}{}^{+}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ then sit on a quinonoid ring, and this protonated quinonoid form is red.

In the titration of a base with an acid, the solution becomes just acidic at the end point, so the indicator changes from yellow to red and is present in the quinonoid form.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: 56.0 L of nitrogen gas is mixed with excess hydrogen gas and it is found that 20 L of ammonia gas is produced. The volume of unused nitrogen gas is found to be $_________ L$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{N}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+3\mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\to 2\mathrm{NH}_{3}(\mathrm{g})$

Since $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ is in excess and $20\mathrm{L}$ of ammonia gas is produced.

Hence, 2 moles $\mathrm{NH}_{3}\equiv 1$ mole $\mathrm{N}_{2}(v\propto \mathrm{n})$

Volume of $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ left $=56-10$

$=46\mathrm{L}$

text: When the excited electron of a H atom from n = 5 drops to the ground state, the maximum number of emission lines observed are $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Maximum number of emission lines

$=\frac{(n_{2}-n_{1})(n_{2}-n_{1}+1)}{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{n}_{2}=5 \\ \mathrm{n}_{1}=1 \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{(5-1)(5-1+1)}{2}=10 \end{array}$

Hence maximum number of emission lines observed are $10.$

text:
While performing a thermodynamics experiment, a student made the following observations.

HCl + NaOH $\to$ NaCl $+ H_{2}O$ $\Delta$H = $-$57.3 kJ mol$^{-1}$

$CH_{3}$COOH + NaOH $\to$ $CH_{3}$COONa $+ H_{2}O$ $\Delta$H = $-$55.3 kJ mol$^{-1}$

The enthalpy of ionization of $CH_{3}$COOH as calculated by the student is $_____________ kJ$ mol$^{-1}. ($nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(I) $\mathrm{HCl}+\mathrm{NaOH}\to \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

$\Delta \mathrm{H}_{1}=-57.3\mathrm{KJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

(II) $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{NaOH}\to \mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COONa}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

$\Delta \mathrm{H}_{2}=-55.3\mathrm{KJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Reaction (I) can be written as

$\text{(III)}\mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\to \mathrm{HCl}+\mathrm{NaOH}$

$\Delta \mathrm{H}_{3}=57.3\mathrm{KJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

By adding (II) and (III)

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{NaCl}\to \mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COONa}+\mathrm{HCl}\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{r}} \\ \begin{array}{ll} \Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{r}}=\Delta \mathrm{H}_{3}+\Delta \mathrm{H}_{2} & =57.3-55.3 \\ =2\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \end{array} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: A sample of 4.5 mg of an unknown monohydric alcohol, R-OH was added to methylmagnesium iodide. A gas is evolved and is collected and its volume measured to be 3.1 mL. The molecular weight of the unknown alcohol is $__________ g/$mol. [Nearest integer]

solution.body:
$\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgI}\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{OMgI}+\mathrm{CH}_{4}$

moles of alcohol $(\mathrm{ROH})\equiv$ moles of $\mathrm{CH}_{4}$

 At STP,
     [Assuming STP]

1 mole corresponds to $22.7\mathrm{L}$

So, moles of alcohol $=\frac{3.1}{22700}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{3.1}{22700}=\frac{4.5\times 10^{-3}}{\mathrm{M}}$

$M\simeq 33\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mol}$
